'''Eberhard Becker''' (born July 23, 1943, in [[Stavenhagen]]) is a German mathematician whose career was spent at the [[University of Dortmund]].  A very active researcher in algebra, he later became rector of the university there.  During his term as rector, it was renamed the Technical University of Dortmund.<ref name=idw>[https://idw-online.de/de/news43458 Prof. Dr. Eberhard Becker succeeds Rector Klein at the helm of the University of Dortmund] Informationsdienst Wissenschaft, 1995-2023</ref>

==Education and career==
Becker received his Ph.D. at the [[University of Hamburg]] in 1972 with the dissertation, "Contributions to the theory of semi-simple quadratic algebra"<ref>German title: Beiträge zur Theorie halbeinfacher quadratischer Algebren</ref> under advisor [[Hel Braun]].<ref name=mgp>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=20995 Eberhard Becker at the Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> He completed his habilitation at the [[University of Cologne]] in 1976.<ref name=catalog>
[https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=nid%3D1047859912 Eberhard Becker] Catalog of the German National Library</ref> In 1979 Becker was appointed to the mathematics department at the [[University of Dortmund]].<ref name=catalog/>

His research included work in the algebraic theory of [[quadratic forms]] and [[real algebraic geometry]].  His collaborators included Manfred Knebusch and [[Alex F. T. W. Rosenberg]].<ref>"[https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0021869385901358  Reduced forms and reduced Witt rings of higher level]" by Eberhard Becker and Alex Rosenberg, [[Journal of Algebra]], Vol 92, Issue 2, Feb 1985, pp 477-503</ref> He supervised over a dozen doctoral students, including Markus Schweighofer, Susanne Pumplün, and Thorsten Wörmann.<ref name=mgp/>

In the mid 1980s, Becker proved that the expression (1 + <math>t^2</math>)/(2 + <math>t^2</math>) was a sum of 4th powers, 6th powers, 8th powers and so on.<ref>published in 1996</ref> He offered a bottle of champaign to anyone who could find explicit representations of this form.<ref>[[Victoria Powers]], "[https://www.jstor.org/stable/2974612 Hilbert's 17th Problem and the Champagne Problem]", [[The American Mathematical Monthly]], Dec., 1996, Vol. 103, No. 10 (Dec., 1996), pp. 879-887.</ref>   [[Bruce Reznick]] came up with a solution in 1994.<ref>Bruce Reznick, "Some concrete aspects of Hilbert's 17th Problem," Seminarie de Structures Algebriques Ordonnees, Vol. 56, Equipe de Logique Mathematique, Universite Paris VII, 1996.</ref>

After working as institute director, dean and member of the Senate at the University of Dortmund, Becker became rector there on April 30, 2002 following the resignation of Hans-Jürgen Klein.<ref name=idw/> During his term in office the Senate decided, at his request, to change the name from “University of Dortmund” to “Technical University of Dortmund”. This decision was not without controversy, particularly in the humanities departments, but was confirmed at the crucial Senate meeting by two-thirds of the vote. On September 1, 2008 he was replaced by [[Ursula Gather]].

On the occasion of his retirement on November 7, 2008, the faculty organized a celebratory colloquium for him.  To mark his 80th birthday, a conference on [[Quadratic form|Quadratic Forms]] and [[Real algebraic geometry|Real Algebra]] was held in October 2023 at the University of Dortmund.<ref name=80th>[http://wwwold.mathematik.tu-dortmund.de/~dplauman//poster.pdf Quadratic Forms and Real Algebra] Conference on the occasion of Eberhard Becker‘s 80th birthday, Dortmund, 26–27 October 2023</ref>
